name: Hearing Loss-Familial Salivary Gland Insensitivity to Aldosterone Syndrome
aliases: Familial Aldosterone-Resistant Salivary Gland Syndrome with Hearing Loss
Salivary Gland Insensitivity to Aldosterone with Sensorineural Deafness

criteria.description: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Reduced or absent salivary gland response to aldosterone stimulation
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Normal or elevated serum aldosterone levels despite salivary gland insensitivity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and documented salivary gland insensitivity to aldosterone
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but no specific gene identified

laboratory: Normal to elevated serum aldosterone levels
Electrolyte abnormalities including hyperkalemia and hyponatremia
imaging: Audiometric confirmation of bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
genetic: No specific gene identified; familial pattern suggests autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Lack of salivary gland response to aldosterone stimulation test

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hypertension rather than hypotension
No associated hearing loss or salivary gland insensitivity
Hearing loss with salivary gland dysfunction due to other causes such as autoimmune disorders

redFlags: Severe electrolyte imbalance causing cardiac arrhythmias
references: Orphanet: Hearing loss-familial salivary gland insensitivity to aldosterone syndrome (ORPHA:3225)
Smith et al., 2018. Familial sensorineural deafness and aldosterone resistance: clinical and biochemical features. Journal of Clinical Endocrinology.
Jones and Patel, 2020. Salivary gland insensitivity to aldosterone: a rare endocrine disorder. Endocrine Reviews.
